issue.title: tailnet.md: warn agents that osascript app-control over SSH to the Mac pops a TCC Automation prompt
issue.description:
Add a short gotcha to `tailnet.md` under the `mac` row/notes: over SSH to the Mac, never
run `osascript` (or JXA) that targets another app (`tell application "Finder"`, System
Events, etc.). macOS attributes SSH-session processes to `sshd-keygen-wrapper` and pops
a blocking TCC **Automation** prompt on the Mac's screen ("sshd-keygen-wrapper wants to
control Finder"), which the user must approve by hand. For screen/display facts use
permission-free sources instead: `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType -json` or JXA
`ObjC.import("AppKit"); $.NSScreen.mainScreen.frame`. Also note that the Mac's login
shell is zsh, where `log` is a builtin: use `/usr/bin/log show` for unified-log queries.

Evidence: on 2026-10-19 12:17:48 EDT bob-cli agent `11v.w0` ran
`osascript -e 'tell application "Finder" to get bounds of window of desktop'` over SSH;
the Mac's tccd logged "Prompting for access to indirect object Finder by
sshd-keygen-wrapper" at 12:17:49 and the user (unsure what it was) approved it at
12:17:58. The same data was available without a prompt via JXA NSScreen one command
later. Full write-up: research:202610/mac_sshd_finder_automation_prompt.md.
